label: Housework and laundry
rationale: The chores beyond the kitchen: housework as a whole, laundry from the line to the drawer, and vacuuming.
mixUps: hosu is you hanging the washing out, kawaku is it drying (sentakumono kawaita?), and folding is tatamu, not oru (paper). 'Vacuum' is a verb in English, but Japanese runs the machine with kakeru: soujiki o kakeru, like mezamashi o kakeru.

targets.verbSense: do; the general verb for tasks and chores
targets.use: Housework as a whole (cooking, cleaning, laundry), mostly in talk about who does what at home: kaji wa futari de yatteru (we both do the housework). Casual speech drops o, and yaru often replaces suru.
targets.notes: Helping with it is kaji o tetsudau; splitting it is kaji o buntan suru.

example.ja: 今日は一日家事してた。
example.english: I spent all day on housework.

examplePolite.romaji: kyou wa ichinichi kaji o shite imashita.
examplePolite.ja: 今日は一日家事をしていました。
examplePolite.english: I spent the whole day doing housework.

targets.verbSense: hang out to dry; air in the sun
targets.trap: English 'hang' points to kakeru, but laundry put out to dry is hosu. The careful noun is sentakumono (the clothes); casual speech often shortens it to sentaku hosu.
partners: futon (futon: air it in the sun)
targets.use: A daily chore in Japan, where most laundry is hung up to dry rather than tumble-dried: out on the balcony, or indoors (heyaboshi) when it rains. sentakumono hoshita? (did you hang the washing out?). Casual speech drops o.
targets.notes: Once it's dry (sentakumono ga kawaku: kawaita?), bringing it in is torikomu (sentakumono torikonde!) and folding it is tatamu (fuku o tatamu).

example.ja: 天気いいから、洗濯物干そう。
example.english: It's sunny, let's hang the washing out.

examplePolite.romaji: kyou wa tenki ga ii node, sentakumono o soto ni hoshimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 今日は天気がいいので、洗濯物を外に干しました。
examplePolite.english: The weather's nice today, so I hung the laundry outside.

targets.kana: せんたくものがかわく
targets.trap: Not sentakumono o kawaku: kawaku is the laundry drying by itself. Hanging it out to dry is sentakumono o hosu; drying something yourself with heat is kawakasu (kami o kawakasu, dry your hair).
targets.use: Comes up with the weather: sentakumono kawaita? (is the washing dry?), and in the rainy season the complaint sentakumono ga kawakanai. Casual speech drops ga.
targets.notes: Washing hung indoors on a rainy day is heyaboshi; a tumble dryer is kansouki.

example.ja: 今日は洗濯物乾かないね。

examplePolite.romaji: kyou wa sentakumono ga kawakimasen ne.
examplePolite.ja: 今日は洗濯物が乾きませんね。
examplePolite.english: The laundry won't dry today, will it?

targets.verbSense: fold up; also close (an umbrella), shut down (a shop)
targets.trap: Not oru: oru is folding paper (origami) or snapping something (hone o oru). Clothes, futons and umbrellas are tatamu.
targets.use: Usually once the dry washing has been brought in (sentakumono o torikomu): fuku tatande (fold your clothes), with sentakumono as the object just as often (sentakumono tatanda?). Casual speech drops o.
targets.notes: Folded clothes then go away with shimau: tatande shimatte (fold them and put them away).

examplePolite.romaji: fuku wa chanto tatande kudasai ne.
examplePolite.ja: 服はちゃんと畳んでくださいね。

targets.verbSense: hang or put something onto something; set a device going
targets.trap: English 'vacuum' is a verb, but Japanese runs the machine with kakeru: soujiki (o) kakeru. Casual soujiki suru is also heard, and soujiki o tsukau (use the vacuum) is fine but less usual.
targets.use: The everyday way to say 'vacuum': soujiki kakeru kara chotto doite (I'm vacuuming, move a sec). Casual speech drops o; souji suru (clean) covers it along with the rest of the cleaning.
targets.notes: The same kakeru irons a shirt (airon o kakeru) and sets an alarm (mezamashi o kakeru).

example.ja: あとで掃除機かけとくね。

examplePolite.romaji: ato de soujiki o kakete okimasu ne.
examplePolite.ja: あとで掃除機をかけておきますね。

get lost (wander off, like a lost child)
